subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory keep advertised OGG/Opus support by adding an owned transcode path, or should OpenClaw narrow provider-aware audio support to Gemini's native MP3/WAV contract?
rationale: Both fixes are plausible, but they carry different product and dependency contracts: filtering/docs is smaller and safer, while transcode preserves advertised support but adds codec and operator behavior.

options.title: Provider-aware validation first
options.body: Skip or reject unsupported Gemini audio formats with clear diagnostics and docs, keeping transcode as a separately approved enhancement.

options.title: Owned transcode support
options.body: Add a tested ffmpeg-backed OGG/Opus to WAV/MP3 normalization path, including dependency handling, diagnostics, and live Gemini proof.

options.title: Docs-only narrowing
options.body: Remove unsupported audio formats from public docs and schema expectations, but this should be paired with runtime diagnostics to avoid raw provider 400s.

recommendation.title: Provider-aware validation first
recommendation.body: Skip or reject unsupported Gemini audio formats with clear diagnostics and docs, keeping transcode as a separately approved enhancement.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner history is closest to the shipped multimodal memory subset and its config/docs boundary.
